findings.issue_text: [ADVISORY] runSplitQuery and runShardSplitQuery now call datasource.applyTemplateVariables(query, request.scopedVars, request.filters) with a third `filters` argument, but the diff contains no change to LokiDatasource.applyTemplateVariables, whose existing signature accepts (query, scopedVars) only. If the production LokiDatasource method was not updated in a companion change, TypeScript compilation of querySplitting.ts/shardQuerySplitting.ts fails against the real datasource type, and if the signature was widened but the implementation ignores `filters`, ad-hoc request filters are silently dropped from interpolated queries; the new tests pass either way only because they mock applyTemplateVariables or inject a stubbed template service, so the real 3-argument call path is never exercised.

[ADVISORY] The new shard test asserts the exact interpolated expr 'count_over_time({a="b", __stream_shard__=~"20|10"} | drop __stream_shard__[5m])', hard-coupling the test to the internal shard-selector regex construction inside splitQueriesByStreamShard, while the interpolation itself is verified only through the stubbed replace() on $__auto/$step. A future maintainer who changes shard grouping or the label-matcher insertion format in shardQuerySplitting.ts gets a confusing failure in a test whose stated purpose is interpolation, not shard formatting; the actual interpolation of the shard selector label values (which goes through a different code path than $__auto/$step) is not covered at all, so a regression dropping interpolation inside splitQueriesByStreamShard breaks users running sharded queries with template variables in the selector.

[BUG] The updated expectation `expect(datasource.applyTemplateVariables).toHaveBeenCalledTimes(5)` for a request with a single target proves that each shard-split sub-query is passed through applyTemplateVariables a second time after the initial map in runShardSplitQuery (line 49-53 of shardQuerySplitting.ts), producing double interpolation of already-interpolated expressions. Any variable value that itself contains template syntax (e.g. a variable whose value is `$other_var` or a `$__` macro) is substituted twice; the user's literal data is silently rewritten in the executed query, and for queries already interpolated once in the map, the shard path re-runs interpolation on the final expr sent to Loki, corrupting queries containing dollar signs.

[BUG] runSplitQuery now unconditionally maps every query through applyTemplateVariables before handing chunked sub-queries to datasource.runQuery, which itself performs interpolation on its targets (the pre-diff code deliberately left interpolation to runQuery, and the diff's own test has to mock runQuery precisely because it is the later execution path), so time-chunked queries get their expr interpolated twice. A variable value containing template syntax or a `$` literal is expanded twice on the chunked path, silently altering the executed expression; the pre-diff single-interpolation contract of runSplitQuery is broken with no test asserting runQuery receives already-interpolated exprs exactly once.

[ADVISORY] The only new interpolation test in querySplitting.test.ts covers the non-chunked path (it inspects only mock.calls[0][0] for a single-request query) and never asserts that time-chunked sub-queries or the shard-splitting sub-queries in shardQuerySplitting receive correctly interpolated expr/step, nor that the third argument request.filters is forwarded to applyTemplateVariables. A future regression where chunked sub-queries drop the interpolated step (or where ad-hoc filters stop being passed) would pass the entire suite; users with dashboard filters or chunked time ranges get un-interpolated `$step`/`$__auto` values sent to Loki and empty or errored panels.

[ADVISORY] The diff changes behavior so that isLogsQuery/querySupportsSplitting and the split-shard label-value fetch now see the interpolated expr, but no test verifies the split-decision functions operate on interpolated expressions (e.g. a `$logs_filter` variable that resolves to a query that does/doesn't support splitting). The routing decision (logs vs metrics, splitting vs non-splitting) can change based on interpolation, and without a test pinning that interpolated expr feeds querySupportsSplitting, a refactor reverting to raw targets would misroute queries containing variable-based selectors, splitting ones that can't be split.

[ADVISORY] runSplitQuery now interpolates every query via applyTemplateVariables and then hands the already-interpolated queries back to datasource.runQuery, which itself performs interpolation in its normal pipeline, so variables are interpolated twice on every split query. Users with non-idempotent template variable transforms (e.g. custom variables with regex or nested variable references whose output contains further variable syntax) get a double-substituted expression — e.g. a variable expanding to '$other' is resolved twice — producing wrong query results or server-side parse errors that only manifest on split-query time ranges.

[ADVISORY] runShardSplitQuery drops its call to datasource.interpolateVariablesInQueries in favor of per-query applyTemplateVariables, changing behavior for queries with empty expr — the new filter drops expr-less queries before interpolation while interpolateVariablesInQueries was applied to all targets, and any downstream consumer of the datasource's interpolateVariablesInQueries path for shard queries is now a silent no-op. Out-of-tree callers or inherited dashboards relying on interpolateVariablesInQueries running for shard-split requests no longer get interpolation through that entry point; also any code that previously received a fresh interpolated query array now shares the same LokiQuery objects mutated in place, so a re-run of the same request re-interpolates already-substituted exprs.

[BUG] The shard path now interpolates every query twice: once in this new map() and again inside splitQueriesByStreamShard (the diff's own test at shardQuerySplitting.test.ts:113 asserts applyTemplateVariables is called 5 times for a single query, proving the per-shard re-interpolation still runs on already-interpolated queries). Any variable value that itself contains '$' (e.g. a regex value like '$^', or '$/' in a LogQL regex filter — extremely common in Loki label-matchers) is re-expanded on the second pass, silently corrupting the executed query; step and expr are also substituted twice, so a variable whose replacement introduces a new template token produces a different query than the non-shard path.

[BUG] runSplitQuery now interpolates via datasource.applyTemplateVariables before passing queries to datasource.runQuery, which itself performs template interpolation on the targets it receives (the pre-diff code deliberately passed raw queries to runQuery so interpolation happened exactly once inside it). Every query through runSplitQuery is interpolated twice; a variable value containing template syntax ('$' in regex filters, literal '$step' text in a log line) is expanded again inside runQuery, yielding a corrupted expr different from what single interpolation produces on the non-split path — the same query renders differently depending on whether splitting engages.

[ADVISORY] runSplitQuery and runShardSplitQuery each own a divergent copy of the filter-then-interpolate pipeline (different filter order, and only the shard version drops non-log/metric concerns downstream), duplicating the query-preparation shape that previously lived in one place (interpolateVariablesInQueries in the datasource). The next change to query preparation (e.g. adding a new filterable field or fixing an interpolation bug) must be made in both files and will drift — exactly the split that caused this diff to fix one path and leave the other with the double-interpolation hazard.

[BUG] runSplitQuery now interpolates queries via datasource.applyTemplateVariables, but in the production path LokiDatasource.query() already calls interpolateVariablesInQueries on request.targets before delegating to runSplitQuery, so every query is interpolated twice. Double interpolation silently corrupts expressions for non-idempotent templates — e.g. a variable whose replacement contains '$' or a $step/'$__auto'-style var whose replacement text is itself re-scanned, or ad-hoc filter segments appended twice — producing wrong query results rather than an error.

[BUG] runShardSplitQuery switches from interpolateVariablesInQueries(request.targets, request.scopedVars) to applyTemplateVariables(query, request.scopedVars, request.filters), so ad-hoc dashboard filters are now applied to shard queries when the replaced call site never passed them. Users with ad-hoc filters on a Loki panel that previously used unfiltered shard-split queries now get silently different (filtered) results after this change — an unaccepted behavior change to the query contract, not just a refactor to a per-query API.

[ADVISORY] Replacing interpolateVariablesInQueries with a direct per-query applyTemplateVariables map discards any wrapper-level behavior the datasource's interpolateVariablesInQueries performs beyond the per-query call (such as instant-query end-time adjustment), without evidence that the two code paths are semantically equivalent. If the wrapper does per-query post-processing, instant or special query types silently lose that handling when routed through the shard-splitting path; the next datasource-side change to interpolateVariablesInQueries will no longer reach these queries, creating hidden coupling between the two interpolation entry points.

[ADVISORY] The .filter((query) => query.expr) guard now runs on raw (pre-interpolation) expressions in both files, whereas the shard path previously filtered after interpolation, so queries whose expr is populated only by template variables are dropped. A panel with an expr built entirely from a variable (expr empty at request time) is silently skipped in the split path and returns no data, while the non-split datasource path runs it — a silent divergence for edge-case dashboards.

[ADVISORY] The mocked applyTemplateVariables mutates the passed query in place and returns it, so the shard tests cannot detect whether runShardSplitQuery uses the map() return value or the mutated original. The real LokiDatasource.applyTemplateVariables is free to return a fresh query object without mutating; the mutation-based mocks make every shard test pass under both contracts, so a refactor of runShardSplitQuery that drops the .map() return (e.g. reverts to filtering the raw targets) passes the entire shard suite while production emits uninterpolated expressions. The 'Interpolates queries before execution' test at line 84 is the only one exercising real replacement; the 'Sends the whole stream selector' test (line 172) and the count-only assertion at line 111 verify the mock, not the interpolation contract.

[ADVISORY] The new interpolation test only covers a query whose classification (querySupportsSplitting, isLogsQuery) is identical before and after interpolation, leaving the reordering of interpolation ahead of classification unverified. The diff changes behavior so that partitioning decisions now run on the interpolated expr instead of the raw expr; a query like '{a="$var"}' or an expr beginning with a variable that resolves to a metric/log query is now classified differently than before the diff. No test in querySplitting.test.ts (checked all tests in the file: only the new 'Interpolates queries before execution' case involves variables) triggers a query whose logs-vs-metric or splitting-support verdict changes as a result of interpolation, so a regression in the interpolation-before-partition ordering ships silently.

[ADVISORY] The new interpolation relies on datasource.applyTemplateVariables covering every templatable field, but the tests exercise it only against the test factory's mock applyTemplateVariables, not the production LokiDatasource implementation, so a field like the metric query's `step: '$step'` that interpolateVariablesInQueries previously handled (or that another code path handled) can silently regress to literal '$step' reaching Loki. A user with a dashboard variable in the step field gets queries executed with an unparsed step (Loki error or wrong resolution) with no client-side error surfaced; the added tests pass because the mock factory's applyTemplateVariables interpolates step, masking whether the real datasource does.

adjudication.rationale: In shardQuerySplitting.test.ts the mock `datasource.applyTemplateVariables` mutates the passed `query` object in place and returns it (e.g. lines where `query.expr = query.expr.replace(...)` then `return query`). Because the same objects from `request.targets` are being mutated, tests that only check call counts (`expect(datasource.applyTemplateVariables).toHaveBeenCalledTimes(5)`) or other behavior can still pass even if `runShardSplitQuery` stopped using the `.map(...)` return value and relied (accidentally) on mutation, or conversely if a future real implementation returns a fresh object without mutating. This is a test-contract weakness rather than a defect in the current production code (which does use `.map(...)` and passes the returned queries).

adjudication_records.issue_text: [ADVISORY] The new interpolation test only covers a query whose classification (querySupportsSplitting, isLogsQuery) is identical before and after interpolation, leaving the reordering of interpolation ahead of classification unverified. The diff changes behavior so that partitioning decisions now run on the interpolated expr instead of the raw expr; a query like '{a="$var"}' or an expr beginning with a variable that resolves to a metric/log query is now classified differently than before the diff. No test in querySplitting.test.ts (checked all tests in the file: only the new 'Interpolates queries before execution' case involves variables) triggers a query whose logs-vs-metric or splitting-support verdict changes as a result of interpolation, so a regression in the interpolation-before-partition ordering ships silently.

adjudication.rationale: The diff changes `runSplitQuery` and `runShardSplitQuery` to call `datasource.applyTemplateVariables(...)` before partitioning/classification (e.g., `partition(queries, (query) => !querySupportsSplitting(query))` and `isLogsQuery(query.expr)`). The newly added interpolation tests assert that `$__auto`/`$step` are replaced, but they don’t exercise a case where interpolation would change the outcome of `querySupportsSplitting` or `isLogsQuery` (e.g., a variable expanding into a logs vs metric expression or into a form that does/doesn’t support splitting). So the finding about missing coverage for the reordered “interpolate before classify” behavior is accurate and specific to this diff, but it’s a test-gap concern rather than a verifiable defect.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [ADVISORY] The new interpolation relies on datasource.applyTemplateVariables covering every templatable field, but the tests exercise it only against the test factory's mock applyTemplateVariables, not the production LokiDatasource implementation, so a field like the metric query's `step: '$step'` that interpolateVariablesInQueries previously handled (or that another code path handled) can silently regress to literal '$step' reaching Loki. A user with a dashboard variable in the step field gets queries executed with an unparsed step (Loki error or wrong resolution) with no client-side error surfaced; the added tests pass because the mock factory's applyTemplateVariables interpolates step, masking whether the real datasource does.

adjudication.rationale: The diff replaces `datasource.interpolateVariablesInQueries(...)` with per-target `datasource.applyTemplateVariables(query, request.scopedVars, request.filters)` in both `runSplitQuery` and `runShardSplitQuery`. The added/updated tests assert interpolation of `expr` and `step`, but they do so using the test helper `createLokiDatasource(...)` (and in other places explicitly mock `applyTemplateVariables`), not the real production `LokiDatasource` implementation. From the diff alone we cannot verify that the production `applyTemplateVariables` interpolates every templatable field (e.g., `step`) that `interpolateVariablesInQueries` previously covered, so the finding is a specific, diff-grounded gap/risk rather than a demonstrable bug.
